title: Two names for the cup
setup_text: People around your child use different languages. A grandparent asks which word to use for the cup at the table.

choices.label: Use both words during meals
choices.outcome_text: Both words found a place at the table. Everyone took turns remembering them.

choices.label: Ask the grandparent to use their own word
choices.outcome_text: A familiar word came in the grandparent’s voice. The family asked what it meant and tried it too.

choices.label: Use the word already common at home
choices.outcome_text: The familiar word stayed in the daily routine. The grandparent shared another word in a story.

title: Faces on the wall
setup_text: A relative offers to print family photographs for the baby’s room. Wall space is small, and both sides of the family have many pictures.

choices.label: Make a small rotating display
choices.outcome_text: A few pictures went up at a time. The family changed them when there was room for a new face.

choices.label: Put up one photo from each side
choices.outcome_text: Two pictures found space on the wall. Other photos stayed in an album within reach.

choices.label: Keep the pictures in an album
choices.outcome_text: The wall stayed clear and the pictures lived together in a book. Looking at them became something to do with a visitor.

title: A visitor at playtime
setup_text: A neighbour offers to bring their toddler over. The suggested time overlaps with your child’s familiar afternoon rest.

choices.label: Meet before the usual rest
choices.outcome_text: The children had a shorter playtime before the house became quiet. Another visit could be planned later.

choices.label: Try the visit after the rest
choices.outcome_text: The visit began later in the day. There was less time together before everyone needed to head home.

choices.label: Meet outdoors for a short while
choices.outcome_text: The children met outside and came home before the afternoon was over. The visit needed a little more packing.

title: Helping at the market
setup_text: Your toddler wants to carry a small bag at the market. The shopping is heavy, and you are trying to get home before the rain.

choices.label: Give them one light item to carry
choices.outcome_text: A small bag had its own carrier. The journey took a little longer, with frequent checks on its contents.

choices.label: Ask them to help choose an item instead
choices.outcome_text: Your child chose an item from the stall while the grown-ups carried the bags. There was still a job to do.

choices.label: Save the carrying for another trip
choices.outcome_text: The bags got home before the rain. Your child helped unpack them once everyone was inside.

title: A call near bedtime
setup_text: A relative who lives far away can call only near your child’s bedtime. Your child loves seeing them, but the calls often run late.

choices.label: Keep the call short and regular
choices.outcome_text: A short call became part of the evening. There was never quite enough time for every story.

choices.label: Make a longer call on a free evening
choices.outcome_text: The family found a less hurried evening to talk. Calls happened less often but had room for stories.

choices.label: Send voice messages during the week
choices.outcome_text: Small voices travelled back and forth at different times. The live calls became less frequent.

title: A seat at lunch
setup_text: Your child asks to sit with a new friend at lunch, but their usual friend expects them to sit together every day.

choices.label: Help them invite both friends
choices.outcome_text: The lunch plan made room for another child. It took a conversation to find a place where everyone could sit.

choices.label: Let your child choose where to sit
choices.outcome_text: Your child made a choice at lunch and talked about it later at home. The old friendship needed another chance to meet.

choices.label: Suggest different lunch days
choices.outcome_text: The week held time with each friend. Your child had to remember which day was whose.

title: The holiday visit
setup_text: Your child wants an extra night with cousins during the school holiday. Your family has an early journey planned for the next morning.

choices.label: Stay another night and leave later
choices.outcome_text: There was one more evening with cousins. The journey started later than planned.

choices.label: Leave as planned and arrange a call
choices.outcome_text: The family kept the early journey. The cousins planned a call for another day.

choices.label: Ask about another visit soon
choices.outcome_text: The extra night did not happen, but a future visit went onto the calendar. It took a few calls to arrange.

title: The weekly envelope
setup_text: Your child asks for a little money to manage without asking each time. The family budget is already planned for the week.

choices.label: Set a small regular amount
choices.outcome_text: A small envelope became part of the week. The family adjusted another expense to make room.

choices.label: Offer money for specific outings
choices.outcome_text: Money was set aside when an outing came up. Your child had less to manage between outings.

choices.label: Plan a short trial together
choices.outcome_text: A trial amount was put aside for a few weeks. The family planned to revisit it after seeing how it worked.

title: The family meal plan
setup_text: Your child wants to choose one family meal each week. There are different tastes at the table and a budget to keep.

choices.label: Give them one meal to plan
choices.outcome_text: One meal on the list came from your child. Everyone worked within the week’s shopping budget.

choices.label: Choose a meal together each week
choices.outcome_text: The meal list had a new conversation in it. Choosing took longer, and everyone could suggest a dish.

choices.label: Let them choose a side dish
choices.outcome_text: A side dish became your child’s part of the meal. The rest of the menu stayed with the usual plan.

title: The familiar walk
setup_text: Earlier, you chose the school close to home. Now your child wants to stop with friends on the walk back, making the journey longer.

choices.label: Agree on one stop each week
choices.outcome_text: One walk home grew longer. The family adjusted the afternoon plan on that day.

choices.label: Keep the walk direct for now
choices.outcome_text: The familiar journey stayed short. Your child looked for another time to meet friends.

choices.label: Plan a short stop with the other parents
choices.outcome_text: A few phone calls helped the families arrange a stop. The walk needed a little more coordination.

title: The longer school journey
setup_text: Earlier, you chose the school farther away. Your child now wants to stay after school for a club, changing the journey home.

choices.label: Try the club on one day
choices.outcome_text: One journey home moved later. The family made room for the club in the week.

choices.label: Find an activity closer to home
choices.outcome_text: The school journey stayed on its usual schedule. Your child looked for a similar activity nearby.

choices.label: Ask another family about sharing pickup
choices.outcome_text: The families discussed taking turns on the longer trip. The plan took some coordination before it began.

title: An old nursery friend
setup_text: When your child was younger, you tried nursery for a few mornings. A friend from that time invites them to play, but the families live apart.

choices.label: Arrange a visit this month
choices.outcome_text: The children met again after some planning. The journey took part of the weekend, and there was plenty to catch up on.

choices.label: Start with a short call
choices.outcome_text: The children heard familiar voices over the phone. The families could plan a visit when the timing worked.

choices.label: Invite the friend to your area
choices.outcome_text: The invitation went out for a visit closer to home. The families still had to find a day that suited both.

title: A picture for the family
setup_text: When your child was a baby, you shared an update with relatives without a photo. Now a relative asks to post a picture of your child’s artwork.

choices.label: Ask your child who can see it
choices.outcome_text: Your child chose an audience for the picture. The relative waited for an answer before sharing it.

choices.label: Share it directly with the relative
choices.outcome_text: The artwork reached one person without going to the whole group. The original stayed at home.

choices.label: Show the artwork at the next visit
choices.outcome_text: The picture travelled to a family visit instead of a group chat. There was time to talk about it in person.
